basis: Retinal pigment epithelial and macular degeneration causes progressive visual loss.
Fibroblastic soft-tissue neoplasm; pleural, peritoneal and other organ locations vary across this umbrella. Paraneoplastic effects are rare.
Vulvar reproductive-organ neoplasm; no axis applies to the umbrella concept.
Peroxisomal beta-oxidation defect; neurodegeneration or neuropathy affects most across the principal subtypes. Hepatic and ocular involvement varies by subtype.
Palmoplantar and periorificial keratoderma, nail abnormalities and corneal epithelial dysplasia define the syndrome.
Severe cardiac pump failure defines the disease; secondary organ dysfunction is not established as intrinsic common damage.
Hereditary neurodevelopmental subtype with intellectual disability in 2/4 patients supports neurologic involvement; schizophrenia alone has no axis.
Inherited skeletal myopathy and defective protein O-glycosylation define the concept; brain and eye involvement is not established across this broad umbrella.
Severe intellectual disability in 3/3 and characteristic limb malformations define major axes. GI and urinary anomaly frequencies are unclear; infections do not prove immunodeficiency.
Hydrocephalus, pulmonary hypoplasia and limb dysplasia define the syndrome; intestinal malrotation and omphalocele occur in 80-99%.
Medulloblastoma is a primary central nervous system malignancy.
Neonatal platelet deficiency; an immune or infectious cause is not inherent to the umbrella.
Viral or bacterial infection directly affects the external, middle or inner ear.
Papillary neoplasm arises within a breast duct; breast has no axis.
Multiple skeletal dysplasias and defining external-ear malformations; earlobe hypoplasia occurs in 80-99%. Hearing impairment is not required for the external-ear axis.
Isolated inherited dilated cardiomyopathy with frequent heart failure; no extracardiac disease is established.
Inflammation of the glans and foreskin is confined to reproductive anatomy; infection or immune mediation is not inherent to all cases.
Inherited sandal-gap toe configuration is a structural foot abnormality.
Destructive keratinizing epithelial accumulation predominantly affects the middle ear and mastoid; rare sinus subtypes do not define the umbrella.
Malignant soft-tissue sarcoma commonly arises in the trunk, pelvis or limbs; extraskeletal origin does not imply nervous-system disease.
Persistent visual-processing dysfunction is neurologic despite the eye-disorder parent. Normal ocular examinations and tinnitus do not establish eye or ear damage.
Pontocerebellar degeneration and congenital contractures define the syndrome; contractures occur in 2/4. Central hypoventilation and neurogenic dysphagia do not establish lung or GI damage.
FKRP dystroglycanopathy causes muscular dystrophy and defective O-glycosylation; cardiomyopathy affects roughly 30-60% in the predominant limb-girdle phenotype. Brain/eye disease is subtype-specific.
Hereditary acral erythema defines skin involvement; dental abnormalities and clubfoot lack frequency evidence for additional axes.
Distal limb contractures, clubfoot and trismus define a musculoskeletal syndrome; mild microcephaly alone does not establish neurologic dysfunction.
